slice: S2g private native program and media notification artwork

other: native JS excludes AudioContext and mixer runtime

cases: Native metadata artwork URI constructed from validated id and account generation, with no credentials or source URI from JS
Real private image through HTTP and verified HTTPS; duplicate native requests share only the last in-memory future
Platform MediaSession bitmap and notification large icon show the correct private account image
Other-account ids return a non-private placeholder or fail, without leaking private account colour
External URI and query rejected, no public fetch fallback
Missing image, invalid bytes and oversized body fail without clearing native login
Invalid image request while native audio is playing leaves actual playback, index and player error unchanged
Logout cancels delayed native fetch; old generation rejected and late response remains cancelled after next account loads its own cover
Existing program queue, occurrence edits, Activity recreation, focus and connection recovery checks retained
initial_failures: First integration: four pixel-exact checks failed because real engine thumb uses lossy JPEG (one point per channel); corrected to three-point channel tolerance.
Account artwork expectations allow the engine placeholder for unknown/other-account ids, with channel-aware private-colour exclusion.
Final integration reran after strengthened privacy assertion, cancelled-job reference cleanup and invalid-artwork-with-active-audio case.
limitations: Development build, not a public alpha or release
Full authenticated routes, acquisition/previews, podcasts/radio, DJ/Live and process-death persistence still pending
Loaded native artwork does not yet invalidate on cover-edit events while the same id/generation remains the last cached URI (including duplicate occurrences)
browser_source_changes: All ui_web sources frozen before unit, Chromium and native APK preparation. Later changes only Kotlin, Java instrumentation and docs. WebKit starts after native integration and Chromium, with emulator stopped, read-only mount and one worker.
